feature: op6893 DPMAIF downlink ring: BAT/PIT programming, downlink interrupt plumbing and a controlled one-ring observation path

image.flash: boot partition only, queued fastboot, then reboot

what_was_added.registers: AO_DL (ao_ul+0x400), PD_DL (pd_ul+0x100) and PD_WDMA (pd_ul+0x300) are derived from the two regions the device tree already describes; INFRA_AO_MEM (0x10002000) is mapped as a fifth named region because the vendor sets one protection bit there.
what_was_added.bat_ring: coherent 256-entry BAT ring, 8 bytes per entry, each entry naming one 1664-byte coherent buffer; entries are re-published in consumption order to keep the ring flowing.
what_was_added.pit_ring: coherent 16384-entry PIT ring, 16 bytes per entry, which is the vendor geometry for this generation.
what_was_added.interrupt: AP_DL_L2TISAR0 status plus the AO_UL APDL mask register and the duplicate mask field inside AO_DL_RDY_CHK_THRES; the line is shared with the uplink through a refcounted request_irq.
what_was_added.controls: dl (counters), dl_regs (flat register dump), dl_start, dl_stop, plus bounded peek/poke/reset windows that only reach the five mapped blocks and only while neither ring runs.

hardware_sequence.step: downlink ring start with the modem at HS2
hardware_sequence.state: bat=256 pit=16384 buf=1664 frg=0/0 pit_rd=1024 bat_wr=0 irqs=0 pkts=0 msg_pits=0 err=0 mtu_err=0 overrun=0 pit_init_stuck=0
interrupt released (no dpmaif line in /proc/interrupts), BAT_INIT and PIT_INIT back to 0, both base and size fields cleared, PIT_STA3 index bit cleared, status latch 0

blockers_found_on_hardware.symptom: PIT_INIT bit31 (NOT_READY) never cleared and AP_DL_L2TISAR0 latched PITCNT_LEN_ERR (bit 3)
blockers_found_on_hardware.cause: the fragment BAT ring was programmed before the PIT ring; only one of the two initialisations can settle in that order
blockers_found_on_hardware.fix: program BAT, then PIT, then nothing else; the fragment ring is not set up at all and the MTU is clamped to one BAT buffer so the engine never needs to split a packet

blockers_found_on_hardware.symptom: PIT_ADD doorbell stayed busy after the PIT init
blockers_found_on_hardware.cause: the PIT init already publishes the ring capacity (remaining count read back as 15359 for an AP index of 1024), so adding the full ring again overruns it
blockers_found_on_hardware.fix: do not add PIT entries at start; only replenish what the drain consumed

blockers_found_on_hardware.symptom: the driver treated a non-clearing PIT ready bit as fatal
blockers_found_on_hardware.cause: both vendor drivers declare this handshake void and merely log it
blockers_found_on_hardware.fix: record it as pit_init_stuck and continue, so the counters decide instead of the driver aborting

blockers_found_on_hardware.symptom: AP index and write index disagreed (1024 versus 0)
blockers_found_on_hardware.cause: the same-board driver keeps the two equal and rewrites one to match the other in its index check
blockers_found_on_hardware.fix: publish both: PIT_INIT_CON3 carries the AP index and PIT_INIT_CON2 the write index, and the software read pointer starts at the value the hardware reports

negative_results: the downlink ring does not depend on the modem being up: the same PIT failure was reproduced with the modem stopped and at HS2
INFRA_AO_MEM bit 10 (the DPMAIF protection bit) was already set by the bootloader (0x00000f3c), so it is not the missing prerequisite
clearing the modem-side reorder register PD_MD_MISC+0x100 did not change the PIT handshake
opening every AP-side clock gate (AP_MISC_CG_EN 0xff) did not change it
PIT ring size 512 versus 16384 made no difference to the handshake
AP index 0 versus 1024 made no difference to the handshake
masking the downlink events before programming did not change it
a vendor-style AO+PD reset returns PIT_INIT to 0 and leaves the modem alive, but the same programming wedges it again, so the ring is reproducible from a known state

modem_side_observation.rb_pit_init: PD_MD_MISC+0x100 reads 0x4000008f once the modem is at HS2, so the modem does configure its own reorder unit before the AP touches the ring
modem_side_observation.lhif_mapping: with PDP active the modem asked for net_if=0 lhif_q=3 (queue 3), so the data queue remains runtime-selected

not_proven: no downlink packet has been received: the counters are all zero because nothing valid has been sent uplink, so the network had no reason to answer
the AP index / write index choice is derived from the vendor invariant, not yet confirmed by a delivered packet
fragment reassembly is not implemented; a fragment PIT would be counted as overrun and dropped
nothing here delivers packets to the network stack: the drain copies a bounded head into a snapshot and recycles the buffers

verification.host_tests: 57 modem suites pass, including the extended DPMAIF formatter test under ASan/UBSan
verification.checkpatch: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 checks on the driver, header and formatter
verification.cold_start_note: the modem handshake occasionally times out with -110 and no exception record; the probe retries a bounded number of full reboots, which has always recovered
